docs.text:
• Zhang, Z., and B.E. Johnson. 2016. Aquatic Nutrient Simulation Modules (NSMs) Developed for Hydrologic and Hydraulic Models. U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center. Section 3.12, pp. 56--58.
  • Stumm, W., and J.J. Morgan. 1996. Aquatic Chemistry: Chemical Equilibria and Rates in Natural Waters, 3rd ed. Wiley-Interscience.
  • Chapra, S.C. 1997. Surface Water-Quality Modeling. McGraw-Hill.

docs.title: Benthic Algae (\(A_b\))
docs.text: Benthic algae (\(A_b\)) represent attached algal biomass growing on or near the bottom substrate, expressed as areal dry-weight density in g-D m\(^{-2}\). NSM1 treats the attached algal community (periphyton, diatoms, filamentous forms) as a single lumped state variable, following Zhang and Johnson (2016), Section 3.4.

docs.title: Role in the Nutrient Cycle
docs.text:
Benthic algae couple the sediment-water interface to the overlying water-column nutrient pools. Growth takes up NH4, NO3, and dissolved inorganic phosphorus from the water column and produces dissolved oxygen through photosynthesis. Respiration and death return nitrogen, phosphorus, and carbon to their corresponding inorganic and organic pools. Unlike floating algae, benthic algae do not settle, but their growth is attenuated by a bottom-density limitation factor that captures crowding and substrate saturation.

Benthic algae experience the PAR intensity at the channel bottom rather than the depth-averaged PAR, and their mortality is partitioned between the water column and the bed using the fractions \(F_w\) (water column) and \(F_b\) (bottom area available for growth).

flowchart LR
    NH4 -->|uptake| Ab
    NO3 -->|uptake| Ab
    TIP -->|uptake| Ab
    Light_bottom -->|photosynthesis| Ab
    Ab -->|photosynthesis| DOX
    Ab -->|respiration| NH4 & TIP & DIC
    Ab -->|death| OrgN & OrgP & POC

docs.title: Governing Equation
docs.text:
The NSM1 mass balance for benthic algae follows Zhang and Johnson (2016), Eq. 3.17, and is implemented in the dAbdt function in src/clearwater_modules/nsm1/processes.py:

\[ \frac{dA_b}{dt} = \mu_b A_b - k_{rb}(T) A_b - k_{db}(T) A_b \]

The three terms represent growth, respiration, and mortality. Benthic algae have no explicit settling sink because they are attached to the substrate. Every rate constant uses Arrhenius temperature correction.

docs.title: Growth
docs.text:
The growth source term is

\[ \text{AbGrowth} = \mu_b \, A_b \]

where \(\mu_b\) is the specific benthic growth rate (d\(^{-1}\)). NSM1 computes \(\mu_b\) from a temperature-corrected maximum rate \(\mu_{mxb}(T)\) attenuated by light (\(FL_b\)), nitrogen (\(FN_b\)), phosphorus (\(FP_b\)), and bottom-density (\(FS_b\)) limitation factors. The model selects between two formulations through b_growth_rate_option:

Option Name Formulation 1 Multiplicative \(\mu_b = \mu_{mxb}(T)\,FL_b\,FN_b\,FP_b\,FS_b\) 2 Limiting nutrient \(\mu_b = \mu_{mxb}(T)\,FL_b\,\min(FN_b, FP_b)\,FS_b\)

The nitrogen limitation factor uses Monod kinetics on the sum of ammonium and nitrate:

\[ FN_b = \frac{\text{NH4} + \text{NO3}}{K_{sNb} + (\text{NH4} + \text{NO3})} \]

The phosphorus limitation factor uses the dissolved fraction of TIP:

\[ FP_b = \frac{f_{dp}\,\text{TIP}}{K_{sPb} + f_{dp}\,\text{TIP}} \]

The bottom-density limitation attenuates growth as biomass approaches substrate saturation:

\[ FS_b = 1 - \frac{A_b}{K_{sb} + A_b} \]

The light limitation factor \(FL_b\) uses the PAR intensity at depth \(h\) (the channel bottom), evaluated with b_light_limitation_option set to half-saturation (option 1), Smith (option 2), or Steele (option 3). The corresponding methods on the BenthicAlgae process are limit_light, limit_nitrogen, limit_phosphorus, and limit_density.

docs.title: Respiration
docs.text:
\[ \text{AbRespiration} = k_{rb}(T)\,A_b \]

Respiration releases nitrogen to NH4, phosphorus to TIP, and carbon to DIC, and consumes dissolved oxygen. The corresponding method is rate_respiration.

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
\[ \text{AbDeath} = k_{db}(T)\,A_b \]

Death transfers benthic algal biomass to OrgN, OrgP, and POC using the stoichiometric ratios BWn, BWp, BWc, and BWa. The fraction \(F_w\) controls how much of the death flux enters the water column versus remaining on the bed. The corresponding method is rate_death.

docs.title: Settling
docs.text: Benthic algae do not have a settling sink in NSM1. The dAbdt mass balance excludes settling, consistent with Zhang and Johnson (2016), Eq. 3.17.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
The default values below come from DEFAULT_BALGAE in src/clearwater_modules/nsm1/constants.py.

Symbol Description Default Units BWd Benthic algal dry weight stoichiometric ratio 100 mg-D BWc Benthic algal carbon stoichiometric ratio 40 mg-C BWn Benthic algal nitrogen stoichiometric ratio 7.2 mg-N BWp Benthic algal phosphorus stoichiometric ratio 1 mg-P BWa Benthic algal chlorophyll-a stoichiometric ratio 3500 ug-Chla KLb Light limiting constant for benthic algae 10 W m\(^{-2}\) KsNb Half-saturation N constant 0.25 mg-N L\(^{-1}\) KsPb Half-saturation P constant 0.125 mg-P L\(^{-1}\) Ksb Half-saturation density constant 10 g-D m\(^{-2}\) mub_max_20 Maximum growth rate at 20 C 0.4 d\(^{-1}\) krb_20 Respiration rate at 20 C 0.2 d\(^{-1}\) kdb_20 Death rate at 20 C 0.3 d\(^{-1}\) mub_max_theta Arrhenius coefficient for growth 1.047 unitless krb_theta Arrhenius coefficient for respiration 1.06 unitless kdb_theta Arrhenius coefficient for death 1.047 unitless b_growth_rate_option 1=multiplicative, 2=limiting nutrient 1 -- b_light_limitation_option 1=half-sat, 2=Smith, 3=Steele 1 -- Fw Fraction of death flux to water column 0.9 unitless Fb Fraction of bottom area available for growth 0.9 unitless { .parameter-table }

docs.title: Couplings with Other State Variables
docs.text:
• NH4, NO3: benthic algal growth consumes inorganic nitrogen; respiration returns nitrogen as NH4.
  • TIP: growth consumes the dissolved fraction of TIP; respiration returns phosphorus as TIP.
  • DIC: growth consumes DIC; respiration releases DIC.
  • DOX: benthic photosynthesis produces oxygen; respiration consumes oxygen.
  • OrgN, OrgP, POC: the death flux (scaled by \(F_w\)) enters these water-column pools; the remainder \((1 - F_w)\) stays on the bed.
  • Alk: growth and respiration modify alkalinity through r_alkba and r_alkbn stoichiometric coefficients.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Benthic algae parameters are supplied through the benthic_algae process configuration. The BenthicAlgae class inherits from FloatingAlgae and adds the density-limitation half-saturation constant. Parameter names below match the from_config signature.

processes:
  benthic_algae:
    time_step: 300          # seconds
    growth_rate_max: 0.4
    growth_rate_correction: 1.047
    growth_rate_option: 1    # 1=multiplicative, 2=limiting nutrient
    respiration_rate: 0.2
    respiration_rate_correction_factor: 1.06
    death_rate: 0.3
    death_rate_correction_factor: 1.047
    nitrogen_michaelis_menton_constant: 0.25
    phosphorus_michaelis_menton_constant: 0.125
    density_michaelis_menton_constant: 10.0
    light_limitation_option: 1
    light_limitation_constant: 10.0
    light_attenuation_coefficient: 1.0
    ratio_chla_carbon: 40.0
    ratio_chla_nitrogen: 7.2
    ratio_chla_phosphorus: 1.0
    settling_velocity: 0.0    # not used for benthic algae

Growth-rate option scope

Zhang and Johnson (2016) describes two growth-rate options for benthic algae (multiplicative and limiting nutrient), and ClearWater implements exactly these two. The floating-algae harmonic-mean option (3) is not applicable to benthic algae. Set b_growth_rate_option to 1 (multiplicative) or 2 (limiting nutrient) in any configuration.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text: • Source: src/clearwater_modules/processes/benthic_algae.py. The BenthicAlgae class inherits from FloatingAlgae and overrides rate, rate_growth, and limit_light to use bottom-layer PAR, and adds limit_density for the substrate-density term.

docs.title: References
docs.text: • Zhang, Z., and B.E. Johnson. 2016. Aquatic Nutrient Simulation Modules (NSMs) Developed for Hydrologic and Hydraulic Models. ERDC/EL Technical Report 16-1. Section 3.4, pp. 20--32.

docs.title: Carbon -- POC, DOC, DIC, POM
docs.text: NSM1 represents the aquatic carbon cycle with three carbon state variables -- particulate organic carbon (POC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) -- plus a closely related bulk organic matter pool, particulate organic matter (POM). This page documents each state variable, the processes that drive its rate of change, the parameters that govern those processes, and how the carbon pools couple to algae, CBOD, nitrogen, dissolved oxygen, and the atmosphere.

docs.title: Role in the Carbon Cycle
docs.text:
Organic carbon enters the water column primarily through algal and benthic algal mortality. Algal death partitions carbon between a particulate pool (POC) and a dissolved pool (DOC) according to the fractions f_pocp and f_pocb. POC is then hydrolyzed to DOC. DOC is mineralized to DIC by heterotrophic bacteria, consuming dissolved oxygen in the process. DIC exchanges with the atmosphere through CO\(_2\) reaeration, is consumed by algal and benthic algal photosynthesis, and is produced by algal respiration, benthic algal respiration, CBOD oxidation, and sediment release.

POM represents fine detrital organic material suspended in the water column. NSM1 tracks POM separately from POC because POM provides a bulk accounting of non-algal organic solids that settle, dissolve, and contribute to the sediment organic pool. POM is also used when POC is not simulated, in which case POM acts as a surrogate for particulate organic carbon (Zhang and Johnson, 2016).

flowchart LR
    Ap[Floating Algae] -->|mortality f_pocp| POC
    Ap -->|mortality 1-f_pocp| DOC
    Ap -->|respiration| DIC
    Ap -->|photosynthesis| DIC_sink[DIC uptake]
    Ab[Benthic Algae] -->|mortality f_pocb| POC
    Ab -->|mortality 1-f_pocb| DOC
    Ab -->|respiration| DIC
    Ab -->|photosynthesis| DIC_sink
    Ap -->|settling rda| POM
    Ab -->|mortality 1-Fw| POM
    POC -->|hydrolysis kpoc| DOC
    POC -->|settling vsoc| POC_bed[Bed]
    POC -->|settling to sediment| POM
    POM -->|dissolution kpom| DOC_POM[Dissolved pool]
    POM -->|burial vb| POM_bed[Bed POM]
    DOC -->|oxidation kdoc| DIC
    CBOD -->|oxidation| DIC
    SOD[Sediment] -->|release| DIC
    DIC <-->|CO2 reaeration| Atm[Atmosphere]
    DOC -->|oxidation consumes| DOX

docs.title: State Variables
docs.text:
Variable Symbol Units Description Particulate organic carbon POC mg-C L\(^{-1}\) Non-living particulate detrital carbon Dissolved organic carbon DOC mg-C L\(^{-1}\) Water-column dissolved organic carbon Dissolved inorganic carbon DIC mg-C L\(^{-1}\) Sum of H\(_2\)CO\(_3\)*, HCO\(_3^-\), and CO\(_3^{2-}\) Particulate organic matter POM mg L\(^{-1}\) Non-algal detrital organic matter (dry mass)

Units for DIC

NSM1 stores DIC internally in mg-C L\(^{-1}\). Several DIC flux terms in the source code divide by 12000 to convert mg-C to mol-C when combining with Henry's Law and CO\(_2\) partial pressure, following equation (3.45) of Zhang and Johnson (2016).

docs.title: Particulate Organic Carbon
docs.text:
\[ \frac{d[\text{POC}]}{dt} = F_{pocp}\, k_{dp}(T)\, r_{ca}\, A_p + \frac{1}{h} F_{pocb}\, k_{db}(T)\, r_{cb}\, A_b\, F_b\, F_w - k_{poc}(T)\, [\text{POC}] - \frac{v_{soc}}{h}\, [\text{POC}] \]

The first two terms are algal and benthic algal mortality. The third term is first-order POC hydrolysis to DOC. The fourth term is gravitational settling.

docs.title: Dissolved Organic Carbon
docs.text:
\[ \frac{d[\text{DOC}]}{dt} = (1 - F_{pocp})\, k_{dp}(T)\, r_{ca}\, A_p + \frac{1}{h}(1 - F_{pocb})\, k_{db}(T)\, r_{cb}\, A_b\, F_b\, F_w + k_{poc}(T)\, [\text{POC}] - \frac{[\text{DOX}]}{K_{sOxmc} + [\text{DOX}]}\, k_{doc}(T)\, [\text{DOC}] \]

DOC gains carbon from the dissolved fraction of algal and benthic algal mortality and from POC hydrolysis. DOC is lost by first-order oxidation to DIC, attenuated by a Monod oxygen-limitation term.

The DOC budget includes the POM dissolution source \(+ k_{pom}(T)\, f_{com}\, [\text{POM}]\) and the denitrification sink proportional to kdnit_tc and NO3, consistent with Zhang and Johnson (2016), Eq. 3.44. Both terms are exposed as named contributions on the Carbon process so that calibration runs can isolate their effect on DOC.

docs.title: Dissolved Inorganic Carbon
docs.text:
\[ \frac{d[\text{DIC}]}{dt} = \text{Atm}_{CO_2} + \frac{k_{rp}(T)\, r_{ca}\, A_p}{12000} - \frac{\mu_p\, r_{ca}\, A_p}{12000} + \frac{k_{rb}(T)\, r_{cb}\, A_b\, F_b}{12000\, h} - \frac{\mu_b\, r_{cb}\, A_b\, F_b}{12000\, h} + \text{DIC}_{CBOD} + \frac{\text{SOD}(T)}{12000\, r_{oc}\, h} \]

DIC receives carbon from atmospheric CO\(_2\) reaeration, algal and benthic algal respiration, CBOD oxidation, and sediment release. DIC is consumed by algal and benthic algal photosynthesis. The divisor 12000 converts mg-C L\(^{-1}\) to mol-C L\(^{-1}\) for terms that couple to Henry's Law.

docs.title: Particulate Organic Matter
docs.text:
\[ \frac{d[\text{POM}]}{dt} = \frac{v_{sap}\, r_{da}\, A_p}{h_2} + \frac{v_{soc}\, [\text{POC}]}{h_2\, f_{com}} + \frac{k_{db}(T)\, A_b\, F_b\, (1 - F_w)}{h_2} - k_{pom}(T)\, [\text{POM}] - \frac{v_b\, [\text{POM}]}{h_2} \]

POM gains mass from algal settling, settling of POC into the sediment layer (converted to dry mass by fcom), and benthic algal mortality that is not routed to the water column. POM is lost by dissolution (first-order, returning material to the dissolved pool) and by burial into deeper sediments.

POM is tracked in the active sediment layer

NSM1 represents POM as the particulate organic matter concentration in the active sediment layer of thickness h2, following Zhang and Johnson (2016), Eq. 3.38. The active-layer formulation captures the temporary storage and dissolution of organic matter that has settled out of the water column, including the burial sink that transfers material to deeper sediments. The water-column source for POM (algal mortality and POC settling) is converted into a sediment-layer concentration through the depth ratio h / h2.

docs.title: POM Hydrolysis and Dissolution
docs.text: The POM dissolution rate at water temperature follows the Arrhenius correction \(k_{pom}(T) = k_{pom,20}\, \theta^{T-20}\). Dissolution returns particulate organic matter to dissolved forms and is the primary water-column loss term for POM other than burial.

docs.title: POC Hydrolysis
docs.text:
POC hydrolysis is a first-order decay that converts particulate organic carbon to dissolved organic carbon:

\[ \text{POC hydrolysis} = k_{poc}(T)\, [\text{POC}] \]

The POC_hydrolysis function in processes.py (~line 2455) does not include an oxygen attenuation term; hydrolysis proceeds at the temperature-corrected rate regardless of DOX, consistent with Zhang and Johnson (2016), Eq. 3.42.

docs.title: DOC Mineralization
docs.text:
DOC oxidation to DIC is attenuated by dissolved oxygen through a Monod term:

\[ \text{DOC oxidation} = \frac{[\text{DOX}]}{K_{sOxmc} + [\text{DOX}]}\, k_{doc}(T)\, [\text{DOC}] \]

When use_DOX = False, the oxygen attenuation is dropped and oxidation proceeds at \(k_{doc}(T)\, [\text{DOC}]\). DOC oxidation is both a DOC sink and a DOX sink; the corresponding DOX consumption is computed in the dissolved oxygen module using the carbon-to-oxygen ratio roc.

docs.title: Algal Photosynthesis and Respiration (DIC)
docs.text:
Photosynthesis removes DIC in proportion to algal growth; respiration returns DIC to the water column:

\[ \text{DIC}_{\text{photosynthesis}} = \frac{\mu_p\, r_{ca}\, A_p}{12000}, \qquad \text{DIC}_{\text{respiration}} = \frac{k_{rp}(T)\, r_{ca}\, A_p}{12000} \]

Benthic algal contributions use the benthic carbon-to-dry-mass ratio rcb and are normalized by depth h.

docs.title: CO\(_2\) Reaeration
docs.text:
The model couples DIC to the atmosphere through a Henry's Law driven flux:

\[ \text{Atm}_{CO_2} = 0.923\, k_a(T)\, \left( \frac{K_H\, p_{CO_2}}{10^6} - F_{CO_2}\, [\text{DIC}] \right) \]

The factor 0.923 approximates \((MW_{O_2}/MW_{CO_2})^{0.25} = (32/44)^{0.25}\) and converts the oxygen reaeration rate to a CO\(_2\) reaeration rate, following equation (3.47) of Zhang and Johnson (2016). K_H is computed from the temperature-dependent formulation of Edmond and Gieskes (1970).

docs.text: Parameter Units Default Description f_pocp unitless 0.9 Fraction of floating algal mortality routed to POC f_pocb unitless 0.9 Fraction of benthic algal mortality routed to POC kpoc_20 d\(^{-1}\) 0.005 POC hydrolysis rate at 20 C kpoc_theta unitless 1.047 Arrhenius coefficient for POC hydrolysis kdoc_20 d\(^{-1}\) 0.01 DOC oxidation rate at 20 C kdoc_theta unitless 1.047 Arrhenius coefficient for DOC oxidation KsOxmc mg-O\(_2\) L\(^{-1}\) 1.0 Half-saturation oxygen attenuation for DOC oxidation pCO2 ppm 383.0 Atmospheric CO\(_2\) partial pressure FCO2 unitless 0.2 Fraction of DIC present as CO\(_2\) roc mg-O\(_2\) mg-C\(^{-1}\) 32/12 O\(_2\) to C ratio for carbon oxidation { .parameter-table }

docs.text: Parameter Units Default Description vsoc m d\(^{-1}\) 0.01 POC settling velocity vb m d\(^{-1}\) 0.01 Sediment burial velocity fcom mg-C mg-D\(^{-1}\) 0.4 Fraction of carbon in organic matter vsap m d\(^{-1}\) 0.15 Algal settling velocity (from algae group) depth m from hydraulics Water-column depth TwaterC C from TSM Water temperature { .parameter-table }

docs.title: Couplings with Other State Variables
docs.text:
• Algae and benthic algae supply the primary source of POC and DOC via mortality and consume DIC through photosynthesis. Algal growth and respiration rates (ApGrowth, ApRespiration, AbGrowth, AbRespiration) are computed in the algae module and passed to the DIC flux terms.
  • Dissolved oxygen attenuates DOC oxidation through KsOxmc and is consumed by DOC and CBOD oxidation (through roc) and by algal respiration.
  • CBOD contributes to DIC through DIC_CBOD_oxidation, which uses kbod_tc and KsOxbod from the CBOD group. See the CBOD page.
  • Sediment oxygen demand releases DIC to the water column at rate \(\text{SOD}(T) / (12000\, r_{oc}\, h)\).
  • POM exchanges mass with POC through settling and with DOC through dissolution, following Zhang and Johnson (2016).

    f_pocp: 0.9

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• The carbon and POM processes are implemented in src/clearwater_modules/processes/carbon.py and src/clearwater_modules/processes/pom.py. Each is a Process subclass that registers its state variables and rate-of-change methods with the VariableRegistry.
    • POM: rate is composed of algal_settling, dissolution, poc_settling, benthic_algae_mortality, and burial.
    • POC: rate is composed of algal_mortality, benthic_algae_mortality, hydrolysis, and settling.
    • DOC: rate is composed of algal_mortality, benthic_algae_mortality, pom_dissolution, oxidation, and denitrification_sink.
    • DIC: rate is composed of co2_reaeration, algal_photosynthesis, algal_respiration, benthic_photosynthesis, benthic_respiration, cbod_oxidation, and sed_release.
  • Default parameter dictionaries are defined in src/clearwater_modules/processes/constants.py as DEFAULT_CARBON and DEFAULT_POM.

docs.title: CBOD -- Carbonaceous Biochemical Oxygen Demand
docs.text: Carbonaceous Biochemical Oxygen Demand (CBOD) represents the oxygen demand exerted on the water column through bacterial oxidation of organic material. NSM1 treats CBOD as a prognostic state variable that couples directly to the dissolved oxygen budget and, through oxidation, to dissolved inorganic carbon.

docs.title: Role in Water Quality
docs.text:
CBOD is the standard water-quality metric for characterizing the oxygen demand of allochthonous (externally supplied) organic loads such as wastewater discharges, stormwater runoff, and non-point source inputs. NSM1 models ultimate CBOD (CBOD\(_U\)). When laboratory data are reported as CBOD\(_5\), users must convert to ultimate CBOD using the group-specific oxidation rate before assigning boundary conditions (Zhang and Johnson, 2016, equation 3.40).

NSM1 can simulate multiple CBOD groups simultaneously, each with its own oxidation and sedimentation rates. This representation allows the user to distinguish organic loads with different decay characteristics (for example, labile versus refractory fractions) without aggregating them into a single pool. The algal contribution to CBOD is not included; autochthonous organic carbon is tracked through POC, DOC, and DIC instead. The user must avoid double-counting organic matter between CBOD and the organic carbon state variables.

CBOD oxidation ceases at low DO

Zhang and Johnson (2016) notes that CBOD oxidation stops when the water becomes anaerobic. The CBOD_oxidation function in processes.py (~line 2370) enforces this behavior through a Monod oxygen attenuation DOX / (KsOxbod + DOX) when use_DOX = True, consistent with the report.

docs.title: State Variable
docs.text: Variable Symbol Units Description Carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand CBOD mg-O\(_2\) L\(^{-1}\) Ultimate CBOD, one or more groups

docs.title: Governing Equation
docs.text:
For each CBOD group \(i\), NSM1 integrates

\[ \frac{d[\text{CBOD}]_i}{dt} = - \frac{[\text{DOX}]}{K_{sOxbod} + [\text{DOX}]}\, k_{bod,i}(T)\, [\text{CBOD}]_i - k_{sbod,i}(T)\, [\text{CBOD}]_i \]

The first term is first-order oxidation attenuated by dissolved oxygen through a Monod expression. The second term is net sedimentation, which represents settling, scour, and flocculation losses that do not exert oxygen demand. External inputs (boundary conditions, point sources, distributed loads) enter the CBOD budget through the host transport model rather than through the process equations.

docs.title: CBOD Oxidation
docs.text:
\[ \text{CBOD oxidation} = \frac{[\text{DOX}]}{K_{sOxbod} + [\text{DOX}]}\, k_{bod}(T)\, [\text{CBOD}] \]

The CBOD_oxidation function checks the use_DOX flag. When use_DOX = True, NSM1 applies the Monod oxygen attenuation. When use_DOX = False, oxidation proceeds at the unattenuated rate \(k_{bod}(T)\, [\text{CBOD}]\).

CBOD oxidation consumes dissolved oxygen and releases DIC. The dissolved oxygen sink is computed in the DOX module. The DIC source is computed in the carbon module through DIC_CBOD_oxidation, which divides the oxygen-demand flux by the carbon-to-oxygen ratio roc and by 12000 to convert to mol-C L\(^{-1}\). See the Carbon page.

docs.title: CBOD Sedimentation
docs.text:
\[ \text{CBOD sedimentation} = k_{sbod}(T)\, [\text{CBOD}] \]

NSM1 treats sedimentation as a first-order loss with a temperature-corrected rate. The default rate ksbod_20 = 0.0 means that, without user configuration, CBOD is removed only through oxidation.

Sedimentation rate, not settling velocity

ksbod_20 has units of d\(^{-1}\) in NSM1: it is a first-order rate constant, applied directly to CBOD as ksbod_tc * CBOD. If you have a measured settling velocity (m d\(^{-1}\)), divide it by the local water depth before assigning it to ksbod_20.

docs.title: External Inputs
docs.text:
CBOD boundary conditions, point source loads, and non-point inputs are supplied by the host transport model. NSM1 does not generate CBOD internally; algal mortality is routed to POC and DOC rather than to CBOD. Users must convert measured CBOD\(_5\) to ultimate CBOD using

\[ \text{CBOD}_i = \frac{\text{CBOD}_5}{1 - e^{-5\, k_{bod,i}}} \]

before setting initial or boundary values.

docs.title: CBOD parameters (DEFAULT_CBOD)
docs.text:
Parameter Units Default Scope Description kbod_20 d\(^{-1}\) 0.12 per-group CBOD oxidation rate at 20 C kbod_theta unitless 1.047 per-group Arrhenius coefficient for oxidation ksbod_20 d\(^{-1}\) 0.0 per-group CBOD sedimentation rate at 20 C ksbod_theta unitless 1.047 per-group Arrhenius coefficient for sedimentation KsOxbod mg-O\(_2\) L\(^{-1}\) 0.5 per-group Half-saturation oxygen attenuation for CBOD oxidation { .parameter-table }

Temperature correction

Both kbod_20 and ksbod_20 are corrected to ambient water temperature using the Arrhenius form \(r(T) = r_{20}\, \theta^{T-20}\), implemented in kbod_tc and ksbod_tc.

docs.title: Couplings with Other State Variables
docs.text:
• Dissolved oxygen (DOX): CBOD oxidation is the most direct CBOD coupling. The oxygen sink term in the DOX budget is \([\text{DOX}] / (K_{sOxbod} + [\text{DOX}]) \cdot k_{bod}(T) \cdot [\text{CBOD}]\), summed across all CBOD groups. Low DO suppresses CBOD oxidation, which can create a feedback loop in which oxygen-depleted water retains CBOD longer.
  • DIC: CBOD oxidation releases carbon to DIC through DIC_CBOD_oxidation. The flux is scaled by 1 / roc and 1 / 12000 to convert from mg-O\(_2\) L\(^{-1}\) d\(^{-1}\) to mol-C L\(^{-1}\) d\(^{-1}\).
  • Organic carbon pools: CBOD does not directly exchange mass with POC or DOC. Users must avoid double-counting; if organic carbon is well characterized through POC and DOC, external CBOD loads should represent only the fraction of organic matter not already captured in those pools (Zhang and Johnson, 2016, Section 3.10).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The CBOD configuration shown below is for a single CBOD group; multiple groups can be declared as a list and are integrated independently:

nsm1:
  cbod:
    kbod_20: 0.12
    kbod_theta: 1.047
    ksbod_20: 0.0
    ksbod_theta: 1.047
    KsOxbod: 0.5
  flags:
    use_DOX: true

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• The CBOD process is implemented in src/clearwater_modules/processes/cbod.py as a CBOD Process subclass:
    • kbod_tc and ksbod_tc apply the Arrhenius correction.
    • oxidation computes the DO-attenuated oxidation rate.
    • sedimentation computes the first-order sedimentation loss.
    • rate sums the sinks; the framework integrates the rate forward in time using the model time step.
  • Default parameters are defined in src/clearwater_modules/processes/constants.py as DEFAULT_CBOD. Multiple CBOD groups are integrated independently with per-group parameter sets.

docs.text:
• Zhang, Z., and B. E. Johnson. 2016. Aquatic Nutrient Simulation Modules (NSMs) Developed for Hydrologic and Hydraulic Models. ERDC/EL TR-16-1. Section 3.8, pp 41--44.
  • Brown, L. C., and T. O. Barnwell. 1987. The Enhanced Stream Water Quality Models QUAL2E and QUAL2E-UNCAS: Documentation and User Manual. EPA/600/3-87/007.
  • Thomann, R. V., and J. A. Mueller. 1987. Principles of Surface Water Quality Modeling and Control. Harper and Row.

docs.title: Dissolved Oxygen (DOX)
docs.text:
Dissolved oxygen (DOX) is the single most important water quality indicator in surface waters. The DOX concentration reflects the net outcome of every biological, chemical, and physical process occurring in the water column and at the sediment-water interface. Phytoplankton and benthic algae add oxygen during photosynthesis and remove it during respiration. Nitrification, organic carbon oxidation, and Carbonaceous Biochemical Oxygen Demand (CBOD) each consume oxygen as microbial populations metabolize reduced species. Sediment Oxygen Demand (SOD) depletes oxygen at the bed. Atmospheric reaeration continuously drives the water-column concentration toward saturation.

NSM1 resolves this balance explicitly by tracking nine rate terms that collectively determine the DOX budget.

docs.title: Role in Water Quality
docs.text:
NSM1 treats DOX as the integrator of all oxygen-producing and oxygen-consuming processes in the water column. NSM1 computes atmospheric reaeration from a user-selectable combination of hydraulic and wind-driven gas transfer formulations. NSM1 computes biotic sources and sinks from the algal, benthic algal, nitrogen, carbon, and CBOD modules, so DOX is tightly coupled to every other NSM1 state variable. Low DOX inhibits nitrification, promotes denitrification, and triggers sediment nutrient release, so DOX also controls the behavior of the nitrogen cycle.

flowchart LR
    Atm[Atmosphere] <-->|reaeration| DOX[DOX]
    Ap[Floating algae] -->|photosynthesis| DOX
    DOX -->|respiration| Ap
    Ab[Benthic algae] -->|photosynthesis| DOX
    DOX -->|respiration| Ab
    DOX -->|nitrification| NH4
    DOX -->|CBOD oxidation| CBOD
    DOX -->|DOC oxidation| DOC
    DOX -->|SOD| Sed[Sediment]

docs.title: Governing Equation
docs.text:
The DOX mass balance, implemented in dDOXdt at processes.py ~line 3095, sums nine rate terms:

\[ \frac{d[DOX]}{dt} = F_{rea} + F_{ApG} - F_{ApR} - F_{nit} - F_{DOCox} - F_{CBODox} + F_{AbG} - F_{AbR} - F_{SOD} \]

Where each flux term has units of mg-O2 L-1 d-1:

Symbol Term Source function \(F_{rea}\) Atmospheric reaeration Atm_O2_reaeration \(F_{ApG}\) Floating algae photosynthesis DOX_ApGrowth \(F_{ApR}\) Floating algae respiration DOX_ApRespiration \(F_{nit}\) Nitrification oxygen demand DOX_Nitrification \(F_{DOCox}\) DOC oxidation oxygen demand DOX_DOC_oxidation \(F_{CBODox}\) CBOD oxidation oxygen demand DOX_CBOD_oxidation \(F_{AbG}\) Benthic algae photosynthesis DOX_AbGrowth \(F_{AbR}\) Benthic algae respiration DOX_AbRespiration \(F_{SOD}\) Sediment oxygen demand DOX_SOD

docs.title: Atmospheric reaeration
docs.text:
NSM1 computes atmospheric oxygen exchange as a first-order relaxation toward saturation:

\[ F_{rea} = k_a(T) \, (DOX_{sat} - DOX) \]

The model computes the combined reaeration rate \(k_a(T)\) from a hydraulic component and a wind-driven component:

\[ k_a(T) = \frac{k_{aw}(T)}{h} + k_{ah}(T) \]

Here \(k_{ah}\) is a first-order hydraulic reaeration rate (1/d), \(k_{aw}\) is a wind-driven gas transfer velocity (m/d), and \(h\) is water depth.

NSM1 offers nine hydraulic reaeration formulas selected by hydraulic_reaeration_option and thirteen wind reaeration formulas selected by wind_reaeration_option. Option 1 in each case uses the user-supplied values kah_20_user and kaw_20_user directly. The other options implement published correlations of O'Connor-Dobbins, Churchill, Owens-Gibbs, Tsivoglou, Thackston-Krenkel, Banks-Herrera, Wanninkhof, and others as functions of velocity, depth, flow, slope, shear velocity, and wind speed at 10 m. The subroutines kah_20 and kaw_20 at processes.py ~lines 50 and 125 enumerate the full set. Both components are corrected to ambient temperature with Arrhenius coefficients kah_theta and kaw_theta (default 1.024).

docs.title: Floating algae photosynthesis and respiration
docs.text:
Photosynthesis by floating algae releases oxygen in proportion to the carbon fixed, with a stoichiometric bonus when ammonium rather than nitrate supplies cell nitrogen. NSM1 computes:

\[ F_{ApG} = ApGrowth \cdot r_{ca} \cdot r_{oc} \cdot \left( \frac{138}{106} - \frac{32}{106} f_{NH4} \right) \]

Here \(r_{ca}\) is the algal carbon-to-chlorophyll ratio, \(r_{oc}\) is the oxygen-to-carbon stoichiometry (default ron = 2.0*32.0/14.0 for nitrogen, roc = 32/12 for carbon), and \(f_{NH4}\) is the fraction of algal N uptake drawn from NH4. Respiration consumes oxygen in direct proportion to biomass respired:

\[ F_{ApR} = ApResp \cdot r_{ca} \cdot r_{oc} \]

docs.title: Benthic algae photosynthesis and respiration
docs.text:
Benthic algae exchange oxygen with the overlying water column, scaled by the benthic coverage fraction Fb and divided by depth to convert areal fluxes to volumetric rates:

\[ F_{AbG} = \left( \frac{138}{106} - \frac{32}{106} f^b_{NH4} \right) r_{oc} \, r_{cb} \, AbGrowth \, \frac{F_b}{h} \] \[ F_{AbR} = r_{oc} \, r_{cb} \, AbResp \, \frac{F_b}{h} \]

docs.title: Nitrification oxygen demand
docs.text:
Nitrification oxidizes NH4 to NO3 and consumes oxygen at the stoichiometric ratio ron (2 times 32/14 = 4.57 mg-O2 per mg-N). NSM1 suppresses the rate at low oxygen using an exponential inhibition factor controlled by KNR:

\[ F_{nit} = \left( 1 - e^{-KNR \cdot DOX} \right) r_{on} \, k_{nit}(T) \, NH4 \]

docs.title: CBOD oxidation
docs.text:
CBOD oxidation already carries units of oxygen demand, so the DOX flux is simply the CBOD oxidation rate summed across all CBOD groups:

\[ F_{CBODox} = \sum_i CBOD_{ox,i} \]

docs.title: Dissolved organic carbon oxidation
docs.text:
Heterotrophic oxidation of DOC consumes oxygen in proportion to carbon respired:

\[ F_{DOCox} = r_{oc} \cdot DOC\_DIC\_oxidation \]

docs.title: Sediment oxygen demand
docs.text:
SOD acts as an areal sink on the overlying water column. NSM1 corrects the 20 deg C rate for temperature with an Arrhenius factor and for low oxygen with a Monod half-saturation:

\[ F_{SOD} = \frac{1}{h} \cdot SOD_{20} \, \theta_{SOD}^{T-20} \cdot \frac{DOX}{DOX + K_{sSOD}} \]

The subroutine SOD_tc at processes.py ~line 216 implements this correction.

docs.title: Dissolved Oxygen Saturation
docs.text:
NSM1 computes DOX saturation from water temperature and atmospheric pressure using the APHA / Benson and Krause formulation. The uncorrected saturation concentration in fresh water at 1 atm is:

\[ \ln DOX_{sat}^0 = -139.34410 + \frac{1.5757 \times 10^5}{T_K} - \frac{6.6423 \times 10^7}{T_K^2} + \frac{1.2438 \times 10^{10}}{T_K^3} - \frac{8.6219 \times 10^{11}}{T_K^4} \]

NSM1 corrects this baseline for ambient pressure and water vapor:

\[ DOX_{sat} = DOX_{sat}^0 \cdot p_{atm} \cdot \frac{(1 - p_{wv}/p_{atm})(1 - \alpha \, p_{atm})}{(1 - p_{wv})(1 - \alpha)} \]

Here \(p_{wv}\) is the partial pressure of water vapor computed by pwv at ~line 2878, and \(\alpha\) is a temperature-dependent correction coefficient computed by DOs_atm_alpha at ~line 2890. The routine DOX_sat at ~line 2901 performs the full evaluation.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Units Scope Description ron mg-O2 / mg-N global DOX Oxygen-to-nitrogen stoichiometric ratio for nitrification (default 2.0 * 32.0 / 14.0) KsSOD mg-O2 L-1 global DOX Half-saturation for SOD oxygen dependence (default 1.0) SOD_20 mg-O2 m-2 d-1 global Sediment oxygen demand at 20 deg C (default 0.5) SOD_theta - global Arrhenius coefficient for SOD (default 1.060) kah_20_user 1/d global User-supplied hydraulic reaeration rate at 20 deg C, used when hydraulic_reaeration_option = 1 (default 1.0) kaw_20_user m/d global User-supplied wind reaeration velocity at 20 deg C, used when wind_reaeration_option = 1 (default 0.0) kah_theta - global Arrhenius coefficient for hydraulic reaeration (default 1.024) kaw_theta - global Arrhenius coefficient for wind reaeration (default 1.024) hydraulic_reaeration_option integer global Formula selector, 1--9 (default 3, Owens--Gibbs) wind_reaeration_option integer global Formula selector, 1--13 (default 2, Wanninkhof) KNR mg-O2 L-1 nitrogen Nitrification oxygen inhibition parameter (default 0.6) pressure_mb mb global Atmospheric pressure used in saturation calculation (default 1013.25, sea level) { .parameter-table }

Calibrate SOD and reaeration to your site

Sediment oxygen demand and reaeration are typically the largest sources of uncertainty in a DO budget. The defaults above are physically reasonable starting values for a temperate lowland stream; calibrate SOD_20, the hydraulic reaeration option, and the wind reaeration option against measured DO time series before drawing quantitative conclusions. The framework validates the YAML configuration at initialization and reports any out-of-range or missing parameters.

docs.title: Couplings with Other State Variables
docs.text:
DOX is coupled to nearly every other NSM1 state variable:

  • Floating algae (Ap): photosynthesis produces DOX, respiration consumes DOX.
  • Benthic algae (Ab): photosynthesis and respiration exchange DOX across the bed, scaled by Fb/h.
  • Ammonia (NH4): nitrification consumes DOX in proportion to ron; the nitrification rate itself is DOX-limited via KNR.
  • Nitrate (NO3): low DOX promotes denitrification, which does not directly consume water-column DOX but shifts the nitrogen balance.
  • Dissolved organic carbon (DOC): heterotrophic oxidation consumes DOX at the ratio roc.
  • CBOD: first-order oxidation consumes DOX directly.
  • Alkalinity (Alk): nitrification and denitrification rates (which depend on DOX) drive alkalinity changes.
  • Sediment: SOD draws DOX from the overlying water column, attenuated at low oxygen by KsSOD.
  • Atmosphere: reaeration exchanges DOX across the air-water interface whenever DOX differs from saturation.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Because DOX depends on many upstream variables and options, a typical configuration must supply reaeration, SOD, and saturation inputs consistently. The following YAML template covers the required entries.

global_parameters:
  use_DOX: true

global_vars:
  SOD_20: 0.5
  SOD_theta: 1.060
  kah_20_user: 1.0       # used when hydraulic_reaeration_option = 1
  kaw_20_user: 0.0       # used when wind_reaeration_option = 1
  kah_theta: 1.024
  kaw_theta: 1.024
  hydraulic_reaeration_option: 3
  wind_reaeration_option: 2
  pressure_mb: 1013.25

dox_parameters:
  ron: 4.571             # = 2 * 32 / 14
  KsSOD: 1.0

Selecting a reaeration formulation

The nine hydraulic options and thirteen wind options differ in their calibration ranges (shallow streams versus deep rivers, low versus high wind). Review the definitions in the hydraulic_reaeration and wind_reaeration helpers and consult the Zhang and Johnson (2016) manual before selecting an option for your application.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• The DOX process is implemented in src/clearwater_modules/processes/dissolved_oxygen.py as the DissolvedOxygen Process subclass. The rate method sums nine contributions: atm_o2_reaeration, algal_growth, algal_respiration, nitrification, doc_oxidation, cbod_oxidation, benthic_growth, benthic_respiration, and sod. Supporting helpers (dox_sat, pwv, dos_atm_alpha, ka_tc, kah_20, kah_tc, kaw_20, kaw_tc, and sod_tc) are exposed as module-level functions for re-use.
  • Default constants: DEFAULT_DOX in src/clearwater_modules/processes/constants.py defines ron and KsSOD. Reaeration, SOD, and pressure parameters live in DEFAULT_GLOBALVARS.

Stoichiometric consistency

The DOX_ApGrowth implementation uses the stoichiometric expression (138/106 - 32 * ApUptakeFr_NH4 / 106), consistent with the Redfield-based derivation in Zhang and Johnson (2016). Verify that the algal and benthic algal C:Chl ratios (rca, rcb) and ammonium uptake preferences (ApUptakeFr_NH4, AbUptakeFr_NH4) are consistent between DOX, nitrogen, carbon, and alkalinity configurations.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Zhang, Z., and B.E. Johnson. 2016. Aquatic Nutrient Simulation Modules (NSMs) Developed for Hydrologic and Hydraulic Models. U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center, Environmental Laboratory. Section 3.10, pp. 49--54.
  • Thomann, R.V., and J.A. Mueller. 1987. Principles of Surface Water Quality Modeling and Control. Harper and Row.
  • Chapra, S.C. 1997. Surface Water-Quality Modeling. McGraw-Hill.
  • Benson, B.B., and D. Krause. 1984. The concentration and isotopic fractionation of oxygen dissolved in freshwater and seawater in equilibrium with the atmosphere. Limnology and Oceanography 29(3): 620--632.

docs.title: Floating Algae (\(A_p\))
docs.text: Floating algae (\(A_p\)) represent phytoplankton biomass suspended in the water column, expressed as chlorophyll-a concentration in ug-Chla L\(^{-1}\). NSM1 treats all phytoplankton as a single lumped state variable, following the aggregation approach of Zhang and Johnson (2016).

docs.title: Role in the Nutrient Cycle
docs.text:
Floating algae are central to the NSM1 nutrient cycle. The model couples \(A_p\) to dissolved oxygen production through photosynthesis, to inorganic nutrient pools (NH4, NO3, TIP, DIC) through uptake during growth, and to organic matter pools (OrgN, OrgP, POC) through death and respiration. Algal biomass also modifies the light field experienced by other plankton through self-shading.

Because \(A_p\) sets the magnitude of primary production, its dynamics drive diel and seasonal patterns in dissolved oxygen, pH, and alkalinity. The model uses fixed stoichiometric ratios (AWd, AWc, AWn, AWp, AWa) to convert between chlorophyll-a, dry weight, carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus pools.

flowchart LR
    NH4 -->|uptake| Ap
    NO3 -->|uptake| Ap
    TIP -->|uptake| Ap
    DIC -->|uptake| Ap
    Light -->|photosynthesis| Ap
    Ap -->|photosynthesis| DOX
    Ap -->|respiration| NH4 & TIP & DIC
    Ap -->|death| OrgN & OrgP & POC
    Ap -->|settling| Bed

docs.title: Governing Equation
docs.text:
The NSM1 mass balance for floating algae follows Zhang and Johnson (2016), Eq. 3.1a, and is implemented in the dApdt function in src/clearwater_modules/nsm1/processes.py:

\[ \frac{dA_p}{dt} = \mu_p A_p - k_{rp}(T) A_p - k_{dp}(T) A_p - \frac{v_{sap}}{h} A_p \]

The four terms on the right-hand side represent growth, respiration, mortality (death), and settling. Each rate constant is corrected for water temperature using the Arrhenius relation \(k(T) = k_{20}\,\theta^{T-20}\).

docs.title: Growth
docs.text:
The growth source term is

\[ \text{ApGrowth} = \mu_p \, A_p \]

where \(\mu_p\) is the specific growth rate (d\(^{-1}\)). The model computes \(\mu_p\) from a temperature-corrected maximum rate \(\mu_{max}(T)\) attenuated by three dimensionless limitation factors: light (\(FL\)), nitrogen (\(FN\)), and phosphorus (\(FP\)). NSM1 provides three formulations selectable through growth_rate_option:

Option Name Formulation 1 Multiplicative \(\mu_p = \mu_{max}(T)\,FL\,FN\,FP\) 2 Limiting nutrient \(\mu_p = \mu_{max}(T)\,FL\,\min(FN, FP)\) 3 Harmonic mean \(\mu_p = \mu_{max}(T)\,FL\,\dfrac{2}{1/FN + 1/FP}\)

The nitrogen limitation factor follows Monod kinetics on the sum of ammonium and nitrate:

\[ FN = \frac{\text{NH4} + \text{NO3}}{K_{sN} + (\text{NH4} + \text{NO3})} \]

The phosphorus limitation factor uses the dissolved inorganic fraction of TIP:

\[ FP = \frac{f_{dp}\,\text{TIP}}{K_{sP} + f_{dp}\,\text{TIP}} \]

Light limitation (\(FL\)) is computed as a depth-averaged integral of the Beer-Lambert attenuated PAR field. NSM1 supports three options through light_limitation_option: half-saturation (Baly 1935), Smith (1936), and Steele (1962). Corresponding v2 method names are limit_nitrogen, limit_phosphorus, and limit_light.

docs.title: Respiration
docs.text:
\[ \text{ApRespiration} = k_{rp}(T)\,A_p \]

The respiration term returns carbon to DIC, nitrogen to NH4, and phosphorus to TIP. The corresponding method is rate_respiration.

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
\[ \text{ApDeath} = k_{dp}(T)\,A_p \]

The death term transfers algal nitrogen to OrgN, algal phosphorus to OrgP, and algal carbon to POC using the stoichiometric ratios derived from AWn, AWp, AWc, and AWa. The corresponding method is rate_death.

docs.title: Settling
docs.text:
\[ \text{ApSettling} = \frac{v_{sap}}{h}\,A_p \]

Settling removes floating algae from the water column at velocity \(v_{sap}\) (m d\(^{-1}\)) divided by layer depth \(h\) (m). The corresponding method is rate_settling.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
The default values below come from DEFAULT_ALGAE in src/clearwater_modules/nsm1/constants.py.

Symbol Description Default Units AWd Algal dry weight stoichiometric ratio 100 mg-D AWc Algal carbon stoichiometric ratio 40 mg-C AWn Algal nitrogen stoichiometric ratio 7.2 mg-N AWp Algal phosphorus stoichiometric ratio 1 mg-P AWa Algal chlorophyll-a stoichiometric ratio 1000 ug-Chla KL Light limiting constant 10 W m\(^{-2}\) KsN Half-saturation N constant 0.04 mg-N L\(^{-1}\) KsP Half-saturation P constant 0.0012 mg-P L\(^{-1}\) mu_max_20 Maximum growth rate at 20 C 1 d\(^{-1}\) kdp_20 Death rate at 20 C 0.15 d\(^{-1}\) krp_20 Respiration rate at 20 C 0.2 d\(^{-1}\) mu_max_theta Arrhenius coefficient for growth 1.047 unitless kdp_theta Arrhenius coefficient for death 1.047 unitless krp_theta Arrhenius coefficient for respiration 1.047 unitless vsap Settling velocity 0.15 m d\(^{-1}\) growth_rate_option 1=multiplicative, 2=limiting, 3=harmonic 1 -- light_limitation_option 1=half-sat, 2=Smith, 3=Steele 1 -- { .parameter-table }

docs.title: Couplings with Other State Variables
docs.text:
• NH4, NO3: algal growth consumes inorganic nitrogen; respiration returns nitrogen as NH4.
  • TIP: algal growth consumes dissolved inorganic phosphorus; respiration returns phosphorus as TIP.
  • DIC: growth consumes DIC; respiration releases DIC.
  • DOX: photosynthesis produces oxygen; respiration consumes oxygen.
  • OrgN, OrgP, POC: algal death transfers particulate organic constituents to these pools.
  • Alk: growth and respiration modify alkalinity through r_alkaa and r_alkan stoichiometric coefficients.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Floating algae parameters are supplied through the floating_algae process configuration. Parameter names below match the FloatingAlgae.from_config signature.

processes:
  floating_algae:
    time_step: 300          # seconds
    growth_rate_max: 1.0
    growth_rate_correction: 1.047
    growth_rate_option: 1    # 1=multiplicative, 2=limiting, 3=harmonic
    respiration_rate: 0.2
    respiration_rate_correction_factor: 1.047
    death_rate: 0.15
    death_rate_correction_factor: 1.047
    settling_velocity: 0.15
    nitrogen_michaelis_menton_constant: 0.04
    phosphorus_michaelis_menton_constant: 0.0012
    light_limitation_option: 1
    light_limitation_constant: 10.0
    light_attenuation_coefficient: 1.0
    ratio_chla_carbon: 40.0
    ratio_chla_nitrogen: 7.2
    ratio_chla_phosphorus: 1.0

Zero-nutrient guard on the harmonic-mean growth option

The harmonic-mean growth option in Zhang and Johnson (2016), Eq. 3.4, is undefined when either \(FN\) or \(FP\) equals zero. ClearWater's rate_growth method sets \(\mu_p\) to zero in that limit, which is the physically correct behavior (no growth without a limiting nutrient). This guard is documented in the function and verified against the harmonic-mean and minimum-Liebig options in the test suite.

docs.title: Nitrogen Cycle -- OrgN, NH4, NO3, N2
docs.text: NSM1 represents the aquatic nitrogen cycle through four coupled state variables: organic nitrogen (OrgN), ammonia nitrogen (NH4), nitrate nitrogen (NO3), and dinitrogen gas (N2). Together these variables track the flow of nitrogen from detrital organic matter through mineralization, nitrification, denitrification, and algal assimilation.

docs.title: Role in the Nutrient Cycle
docs.text:
The NSM1 nitrogen cycle follows the canonical progression OrgN -> NH4 -> NO3 -> N2. Algal and benthic algal mortality release nitrogen to the OrgN pool. Heterotrophic bacteria hydrolyze OrgN to NH4 (mineralization). Nitrifying bacteria oxidize NH4 to NO3 (nitrification), consuming dissolved oxygen. Under low-oxygen conditions, denitrifiers reduce NO3 to dinitrogen gas (N2), which provides an anaerobic nitrogen sink to the atmosphere. Floating and benthic algae assimilate both NH4 and NO3 for growth, with preference controlled by the ammonia preference factor. Bed release supplies additional NH4, and sediment denitrification removes NO3.

flowchart LR
    Algae[Floating Algae Ap] -->|death| OrgN
    BAlgae[Benthic Algae Ab] -->|death| OrgN
    OrgN -->|mineralization| NH4
    OrgN -->|settling| Bed1[Bed]
    Bed2[Bed] -->|diffusion| NH4
    NH4 -->|nitrification| NO3
    NH4 -->|uptake| Algae
    NH4 -->|uptake| BAlgae
    NO3 -->|uptake| Algae
    NO3 -->|uptake| BAlgae
    NO3 -->|water-column denitrification| N2
    NO3 -->|sediment denitrification| N2
    Algae -->|respiration| NH4
    BAlgae -->|respiration| NH4
    N2 -->|degassing| Atm[Atmosphere]

docs.title: State Variables
docs.text: Symbol Units Description OrgN mg-N L\(^{-1}\) Dissolved and particulate organic nitrogen NH4 mg-N L\(^{-1}\) Ammonium plus ammonia nitrogen NO3 mg-N L\(^{-1}\) Nitrate plus nitrite nitrogen N2 mg-N L\(^{-1}\) Dinitrogen gas (tracked when use_N2 = True)

docs.title: Governing Equations
docs.text:
The rate of change of each nitrogen state variable is the net balance of its source and sink terms. The organic nitrogen budget accounts for algal death inputs, mineralization loss, and settling to the bed:

\[ \frac{d\,\mathrm{OrgN}}{dt} = r_{na}\,k_{dp}\,A_p \;+\; \frac{r_{nb}\,F_w\,F_b\,k_{db}\,A_b}{h} \;-\; k_{on}(T)\,\mathrm{OrgN} \;-\; \frac{v_{son}}{h}\,\mathrm{OrgN} \]

The ammonium budget sums mineralization inflow, bed release, algal respiration inflow, and subtracts nitrification and algal assimilation:

\[ \frac{d\,\mathrm{NH4}}{dt} = k_{on}(T)\,\mathrm{OrgN} \;-\; f_{NR}\,k_{nit}(T)\,\mathrm{NH4} \;+\; \frac{r_{NH4}(T)}{h} \;+\; r_{na}\,k_{rp}\,A_p \;-\; P_N\,r_{na}\,\mu_p\,A_p \;+\; \frac{r_{nb}\,F_b\,k_{rb}\,A_b}{h} \;-\; \frac{P_{Nb}\,r_{nb}\,F_b\,\mu_b\,A_b}{h} \]

The nitrate budget gains nitrogen from nitrification and loses it to water-column denitrification, sediment denitrification, and algal uptake of the nitrate fraction:

\[ \frac{d\,\mathrm{NO3}}{dt} = f_{NR}\,k_{nit}(T)\,\mathrm{NH4} \;-\; \left(1 - \frac{\mathrm{DOX}}{\mathrm{DOX} + K_{sOxdn}}\right) k_{dnit}(T)\,\mathrm{NO3} \;-\; \frac{v_{NO3}(T)}{h}\,\mathrm{NO3} \;-\; (1-P_N)\,r_{na}\,\mu_p\,A_p \;-\; \frac{(1-P_{Nb})\,r_{nb}\,F_b\,\mu_b\,A_b}{h} \]

The dinitrogen budget receives mass from water-column and sediment denitrification and loses mass through gas transfer to the atmosphere.

In these expressions \(h\) is water depth, \(T\) is water temperature, and rate constants suffixed with \((T)\) are Arrhenius-corrected as \(k_{20}\,\theta^{T-20}\).

docs.title: Mineralization (OrgN -> NH4)
docs.text:
Organic nitrogen is hydrolyzed to ammonium at a first-order, temperature-corrected rate:

\[ \mathrm{OrgN\_NH4\_Decay} = k_{on}(T)\,\mathrm{OrgN} \]

The temperature correction uses the kon_20 rate constant and kon_theta Arrhenius coefficient. This flux appears as a sink in the dOrgNdt equation and as a source in dNH4dt.

docs.title: Organic Nitrogen Settling
docs.text:
Particulate organic nitrogen settles from the water column to the bed at velocity vson:

\[ \mathrm{OrgN\_Settling} = \frac{v_{son}}{h}\,\mathrm{OrgN} \]

docs.title: Nitrification (NH4 -> NO3)
docs.text:
Autotrophic nitrification oxidizes ammonium to nitrate. The model includes a low-oxygen inhibition factor NitrificationInhibition that multiplies the first-order nitrification rate:

\[ f_{NR} = 1 - e^{-K_{NR}\,\mathrm{DOX}} \] \[ \mathrm{NH4\_Nitrification} = f_{NR}\,k_{nit}(T)\,\mathrm{NH4} \]

When use_DOX is false, the inhibition factor is set to 1.0. The nitrification rate constant is knit_20 with Arrhenius coefficient knit_theta. The inhibition half-coefficient KNR controls how sharply nitrification shuts down as DOX approaches zero.

Inhibition form

Zhang and Johnson (2016) present the nitrification inhibition term as an exponential of the form \(1 - e^{-K_{NR}\,\mathrm{DOX}}\). The NitrificationInhibition function in processes.py (~line 1422) implements this exact form, consistent with the report.

docs.title: Bed Release of NH4
docs.text:
The sediment bed supplies ammonium to the overlying water at a temperature-corrected areal flux rnh4_tc, distributed over the water depth:

\[ \mathrm{NH4fromBed} = \frac{r_{NH4}(T)}{h} \]

The rate rnh4_20 has default 0 in DEFAULT_NITROGEN, so users must override this value to enable benthic ammonium flux when the sediment flux module is disabled.

docs.title: Denitrification (NO3 -> N2)
docs.text:
Water-column denitrification proceeds only under oxygen-limited conditions. The model applies a Monod-type oxygen inhibition:

\[ \mathrm{NO3\_Denit} = \left(1 - \frac{\mathrm{DOX}}{\mathrm{DOX} + K_{sOxdn}}\right) k_{dnit}(T)\,\mathrm{NO3} \]

The denitrification rate constant is kdnit_20 with Arrhenius coefficient kdnit_theta. The half-saturation oxygen inhibition constant KsOxdn determines the oxygen level at which denitrification reaches half of its anoxic maximum.

Sediment denitrification represents NO3 diffusing into the anoxic sediment bed where it is reduced to N2:

\[ \mathrm{NO3\_BedDenit} = \frac{v_{NO3}(T)}{h}\,\mathrm{NO3} \]

The mass transfer velocity vno3_20 (default 0) must be set to a positive value for this flux to be active.

N2 prognostic budget

N2 is a prognostic state variable with source terms from water-column and sediment denitrification and a sink term from atmospheric degassing. The dN2dt rate function and the N2 reaeration coefficient kaN2_20 follow Zhang and Johnson (2016), Section 3.5. N2 is rarely used in practical applications but is exposed for completeness; if you do not need it, set use_N2: false to skip its integration.

docs.title: Algal Uptake
docs.text:
Both floating and benthic algae draw nitrogen from the NH4 and NO3 pools in proportion to the ammonia preference factors PN (floating) and PNb (benthic):

\[ \mathrm{NH4\_ApGrowth} = P_N \cdot r_{na}\,\mu_p\,A_p \] \[ \mathrm{NO3\_ApGrowth} = (1 - P_N)\,r_{na}\,\mu_p\,A_p \]

Analogous expressions apply to benthic algae using PNb, rnb, the benthic growth rate, the fraction of benthic area Fb, and the depth normalization 1/h.

docs.title: Algal Respiration and Death
docs.text:
Floating and benthic algae return nitrogen to the NH4 and OrgN pools during respiration and mortality:

\[ \mathrm{NH4\_ApRespiration} = r_{na}\,k_{rp}\,A_p, \qquad \mathrm{ApDeath\_OrgN} = r_{na}\,k_{dp}\,A_p \]

Benthic algal contributions include the fraction Fw that enters the water column on death and are normalized by depth.

docs.text:
All defaults are taken from DEFAULT_NITROGEN in src/clearwater_modules/nsm1/constants.py.

docs.title: Couplings with Other State Variables
docs.text:
• Floating algae (Ap): Algal growth withdraws NH4 and NO3; algal respiration returns NH4; algal death supplies OrgN.
  • Benthic algae (Ab): Same couplings as floating algae, scaled by Fb, Fw, and depth.
  • Dissolved oxygen (DOX): Nitrification consumes DOX through the stoichiometric ratio ron (see the Dissolved Oxygen page). Low DOX inhibits nitrification and activates denitrification.
  • Alkalinity (Alk): Nitrification decreases alkalinity through r_alkn; denitrification increases alkalinity through r_alkden; algal uptake of NH4 versus NO3 affects alkalinity through r_alkaa, r_alkan, r_alkba, and r_alkbn.

  use_OrgN: true
  use_NH4: true
  use_NO3: true
  use_N2: true

  # Rate constants at 20 C
  kon_20: 0.1
  knit_20: 0.1
  kdnit_20: 0.002

  # Arrhenius coefficients
  kon_theta: 1.074
  knit_theta: 1.083
  kdnit_theta: 1.08

  # Oxygen inhibition
  KNR: 0.6
  KsOxdn: 0.1

  rnh4_20: 0.05
  rnh4_theta: 1.047
  vno3_20: 0.1
  vno3_theta: 1.045

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Source: src/clearwater_modules/processes/nitrogen.py. The Nitrogen process class implements the OrgN, NH4, NO3, and N2 rate functions, with helpers for nitrification inhibition, bed release, water-column denitrification, and sediment denitrification.
  • Temperature-correction helpers apply the standard Arrhenius form rc20 * theta^(T - 20) from clearwater_modules.kinetics.arrhenius_correction.
  • Diagnostic totals exposed by the process include DIN = NH4 + NO3, TON = OrgN + rna * Ap, TKN = NH4 + TON, and TN = DIN + TON.

Sediment fluxes are disabled by default

The nitrogen defaults rnh4_20 = 0 and vno3_20 = 0 disable the sediment ammonium release and sediment denitrification fluxes. Set both to positive site-specific values when bed exchange is significant for your application.
